claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name(s) of the child or children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for **Alex**.

To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now, to continue the assessment, I need to understand your living situation.

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask about your residency status.

**What is your current immigration or residency status in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, EU citizen, visa holder, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to ask about Alex's residency.

**Is Alex also a British citizen, or does Alex have a different immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is also a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to ask about your work and income situation.

**Are you currently working, and if so, are you receiving any income from employment or self-employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am working.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. To assess your eligibility fully, I need to understand your income level.

**What is your approximate annual income from work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly, but I do work full-time if that matters for eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly fine - whether you work full-time or part-time doesn't affect your Child Benefit eligibility. What does matter for eligibility is your income level, as there are income thresholds that apply.

To clarify: **Is your annual income over £60,000?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, my income is under £60,000.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question to complete my assessment.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and do you live with Alex in your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me review the criteria for Child Benefit and provide you with an outcome.

Based on what you've told me:
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old, a British citizen, and lives with you
- You are working with an income under £60,000
- Alex is in your care and lives with you in your household

You meet all the key eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To summarize your eligibility:
- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✅ You are a British citizen and resident in the UK
- ✅ Alex is a British citizen
- ✅ Alex lives with you and is in your care
- ✅ Your income is under £60,000, so no High Income Child Benefit Charge applies

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already done so, you can apply through the UK government's Child Benefit application process.
